# Finding ∫ -3*x**4*sin(x) dx

I'll use **repeated integration by parts** (tabular method).

## Setting up the table

| Differentiate (u) | Integrate (dv) |
|---|---|
| x**4 | -3*sin(x) |
| 4*x**3 | 3*cos(x) |
| 12*x**2 | 3*sin(x) |
| 24*x | -3*cos(x) |
| 24 | -3*sin(x) |
| 0 | 3*cos(x) |

## Combining terms (alternating signs +, −, +, −, +)

$$\int -3x^4\sin x\,dx = (+)(x^4)(3\cos x) + (-)(4x^3)(3\sin x) + (+)(12x^2)(-3\cos x) + (-)(24x)(-3\sin x) + (+)(24)(3\cos x) + C$$

$$= 3x^4\cos x - 12x^3\sin x - 36x^2\cos x + 72x\sin x + 72\cos x + C$$

## Verification (differentiate the result)

- d/dx[3*x**4*cos(x)] = 12*x**3*cos(x) - 3*x**4*sin(x)
- d/dx[-12*x**3*sin(x)] = -36*x**2*sin(x) - 12*x**3*cos(x)
- d/dx[-36*x**2*cos(x)] = -72*x*cos(x) + 36*x**2*sin(x)
- d/dx[72*x*sin(x)] = 72*sin(x) + 72*x*cos(x)
- d/dx[72*cos(x)] = -72*sin(x)

All intermediate terms cancel, leaving **-3*x**4*sin(x)** ✓

<answer>3*x**4*cos(x) - 12*x**3*sin(x) - 36*x**2*cos(x) + 72*x*sin(x) + 72*cos(x) + C</answer>
